answer: Sybil keys run by one operator tend to move in lockstep, so the ledger can watch timing. If forty agents submit within the same few seconds every epoch, idle at the same nadir overnight and wake together, they look less like independent actors than lines of one sonnet. The network folds such correlated clusters into one identity for rewards and voting, so a farm that ships its keys out from a single wharf of servers gains nothing by cloning them.
